text:
Brandon Montour has been Seattle's offense from the back end in a season when the Kraken have needed the help. He scored the winner in the final minute against Toronto on Oct. 28, and Kraken contributor Alison Lukan called him "a tone setter" after the overtime win over Calgary this week. Eleven points in 14 games is a big jump from last season's 32 in 64, and his ice time has climbed past 24 minutes.

Most of that jump is borrowed. Seattle has scored 6.5 goals more than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and he is shooting 12.5%, about double his usual rate. At 5v5 the Kraken are under water with him out there (48% of the chances), though better than without him. Last season was the reverse: Evolving-Hockey had him producing chances worth far more than his goals showed, with some of the weakest teammates of any defenseman. So think of this as last year's bad luck paying out in one stretch. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him as a strong setup man, and his skating bursts rank near the top of the league. Our projection: about 50 points.
headline: Montour's hot start is last year's luck repaid
